cards.explanation: The answer is True. John 12:2 says Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Jesus. This is the man Jesus had raised from the dead, and now he's reclining at a dinner table. I think that's the best seat in the house.
The answer is feet. Mary anointed Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair (John 12:3). Feet, friends! Not a dab on the forehead, not a quick splash on the hands. She went low and she went all in.
The answer is betray. John 12:4 says Judas Iscariot was going to betray Jesus. The writer tells us that right as Judas opens his mouth. So when the question comes out, we already know who is asking.

The answer is the poor. Judas asks why the perfume wasn't sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor (John 12:5). On the surface, it sounds like a caring question. But the next verse tells us what was really going on.

The answer is thief. John 12:6 says Judas didn't say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. The question sounded nice, but the writer tells us what was underneath it, friends. A nice sentence can hide a lot.

The answer is that he keeps the money bag. John 12:6 says Judas was the keeper of the money bag, and he used to take from what was put into it. Out of everything the group could have trusted him with, that's the job he had. A thief watching the cash, that's a problem.
The answer is that Jesus tells Judas to leave her alone. Jesus replies, "Leave her alone…" (John 12:7). He doesn't scold Mary or argue with the numbers. He just steps in and speaks up for her.

The answer is burial. Jesus says, "She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial." (John 12:7). That's a heavy word, and Jesus says it plainly. Mary's gift, in His words, is tied to that day.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me." (John 12:8). The first part is true, but the second part flips it. They will not always have Him.

The answer is Lazarus. The crowd came not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead (John 12:9). People were coming to see a man Jesus had raised from the dead, friends. I'd be hiding in the pantry.

The answer is kill him, and it's a heavy one. John 12:10 says the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well. I think this is a hard verse to read, so I'll just say it plainly. They wanted him dead.

The answer is True. John 12:11 says that on account of Lazarus, many of the Jews were deserting the chief priests and believing in Jesus. That's the reason the text gives for the chief priests' plan. Lazarus was a living sign of what Jesus had done.
